mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday trips are being replaced by home-based activity and discretionary shopping weakens further, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4-week mean while WORKPLACES remains below zero and RESIDENTIAL remains above zero for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT over one week reduces access to shopping corridors and lowers spontaneous retail visits, so RETAIL_REC decreases within two weeks after the transit shock.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 5 points week-on-week from its prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT drop of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains strongly positive while PARKS stay negative, trips are concentrated in essential errands rather than discretionary outings, and retail-and-recreation mobility stays below the recent average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds above its last 4-week mean despite GROCERY_PHARM staying positive and PARKS staying negative throughout the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply below baseline, the city is operating under a mobility-restrictive regime that suppresses shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC continues to fall over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both below -20 points for at least two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -20 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS activity diverts leisure time away from malls and restaurants, so retail-and-recreation mobility weakens within one week and stays lower for two weeks after the park surge.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by 5 points or more from the prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days after a PARKS increase of at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES remain weak, daytime out-of-home demand is structurally suppressed, and retail visits continue to drift down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and WORKPLACES stays below baseline for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after a prior spike signals post-stockup normalization; once the stockup effect fades, discretionary retail demand improves over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines for two consecutive weekly means after being above 45 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last 4-week mean over the next 14 days even after GROCERY_PHARM falls for two straight weeks from above 45.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers while WORKPLACES remain depressed, commuting resumes without a matching retail rebound, so RETAIL_REC stays flat to lower over the next four weeks rather than improving.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points while WORKPLACES remain below -15 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above its last 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT recovering by 5 points or more while WORKPLACES stay below -15.
